_note: Pairs that are not wrong for each other on one dial (judge findings 5 and 6, Step 8 finding 6), and one-way rules (Step 8 finding 1). Words are copied from book-vocabulary.json by id. Local to Sentence Lock; the shared confusable-pairs.json is untouched.

sameMeaning.why: the two words can each say "very" after an adjective (Lesson 3 line 83: "He is very angry")
the two words can each say "hard" after a verb (Lesson 3 line 72; Lesson 23 lines 171 and 212: "study hard")

the table glosses the first "still, continuing" and the second "currently, in progress" (Lesson 22 lines 190 and 193); the two overlap, so neither is a sure wrong answer for the other (Step 8: both became dials with the table meanings)
the book uses the first for finished work too (Lesson 45 lines 148 and 270: "When the work is done"), so it can also say "finished" (judge finding 6, Lessons 41-52; native-speaker queue item 46)

aSome.why: the two articles both translate English "a" and "some" when the noun has no final accent (Lesson 18 lines 14 and 16; Lesson 8 line 13)

oneWay.why: the book says the first covers the jobs of the other two ("Ē often covers the jobs of all three", Lesson 12 line 51; Lesson 16 line 110), so it can also render "this" and "that near you"; the other direction stays fair (judge finding 1)
